pk.context: 1 mg oral, steady state, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: Tablet bioavailability is 100% relative to solution; a high-fat meal reduces exposure by 18-20%. Only about 13% binds serum proteins, and the kidney eliminates 62-73% unchanged.
clues.substance: The active moiety has a molecular weight of 277.28. It is a powder that is slightly soluble in water, at 2.4 mg/mL.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as 0.5 mg and 1 mg tablets and a 0.05 mg/mL oral solution, dosed once daily.
clues.safety: A boxed warning covers severe acute exacerbations after stopping therapy and lactic acidosis. No contraindications; headache, fatigue, dizziness and nausea are the common reactions.
clues.indication: Chronic hepatitis B virus infection with evidence of active viral replication, in adults and in children 2 years and older.
clues.mechanism: Its triphosphate form competes with deoxyguanosine triphosphate to block all three activities of the HBV reverse transcriptase, and weakly inhibits cellular DNA polymerases.

tell: A deoxyguanosine analogue whose 1 mg tablet is pink and triangular, and is mostly cleared unchanged by the kidney.
